questions: Do you have a known history of diabetes?
Have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your feet recently?
Do you experience pain when walking on your heels?
Is the weakness in your legs symmetrical (affecting both sides equally)?
results: 1. nerve conduction studies: demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy
2. whole exome sequencing: heterozygous likely pathogenic FBLN5 c.1117C>T (p.Arg373Cys) - CMT1H
3. MRI brain with contrast: bilateral contrast enhancement and THICKENING of cranial nerves III through XII
4. MRI spine: symmetrical thickening of the lumbosacral nerve roots
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1H (CMT1H) caused by a heterozygous pathogenic variant in the FBLN5 gene

ALTERNATIVES:
1. Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) with hypertrophic nerve roots and cranial nerve involvement
2. Neurolymphomatosis or perineural spread of malignancy
dx: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1H (CMT1H) caused by a heterozygous pathogenic variant in the FBLN5 gene
